task_name: The channel, end to end over one real process

rubric.result: The objective promises one test driving the four acceptance criteria through the real routes over a real PTY. Taken apart: (1) the session is listed - `RunningApi.listed(port)` hits `GET /sessions` over real HTTP and asserts the literal body `{sessions:[{id,name}]}` built from the session `PtyLiveSessions.open()` really returned; (2) the stream carries what the process printed - `SseFrames.openedOn` opens `GET /sessions/:id/stream`, the first frame (the scrollback that `session-stream-route.ts:43` always writes) is consumed and discarded, so every byte `Echo.reachesTheStream` accumulates comes from a later frame, i.e. from `PtyLiveSessions.#received`; (3) typed input reaches the process - `POST /sessions/:id/input` answers 202 `{status:'typed',id}` and the token comes back out of the pty afterwards, so a no-op `write` would leave the token never arriving and the 30s budget would reject; (4) aborting leaves the session listed and live - test 2 cancels the reader, re-asks `GET /sessions`, then types again and a SECOND subscription receives the token, which proves more than the criterion asks (the process is alive AND the scrollback replays). The spawn is the real `node-pty` (`import { spawn } from 'node-pty'`), the server is a real `ApiServer` on port 0, and the file carries the `-real-process` suffix that `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` makes the marker for the excluded fast subset. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The brief's line reads `**TDD:** No TDD - an end-to-end is written after the behaviours it binds, and it is still red before this slice starts, because `GET /sessions` does not exist on `main`.` There is no assertion the plan fixed for this item to compare against, so it produces no finding. The amendment did not touch that line.

The brief as dispatched declares no `Contract`, `Current state` or `Call site` block for task 10. The amendment introduces one, `Contract (plugin/scripts/ct-step.mjs):` holding `  const declared = t.files.filter((f) => f.path !== planRelPath())`, and I compared it symbol by symbol against the diff: `ct-step.mjs:1478` is that line verbatim, same indentation, same identifier `declared`, same predicate, same call `planRelPath()`. No other signature, error, message or constant is declared anywhere in the task's text, and the diff introduces no exported symbol of its own (the new backend file is a test; its four helper types are local to it). Note for the record: this contract was written by the implementer in the same diff it describes, so it pins rather than constrains - which is why I judged the change itself on its merits under `alcance` instead of resting on the block.

Rows the diff bears on, each checked against the code: P-1 (the port is synchronous) - the test calls `liveSessions.open()`, `.all()` and the use cases without a promise and the stream route writes its headers before the first byte; P-2 (a frame carries bytes and nothing else) - `type StreamedFrame = { bytes: string }` and `SseFrames.bytesOf` reads only `.bytes`, no `kind` is introduced; P-4 (node-pty) - the real `spawn` is imported from `node-pty`, no version is touched; P-6 (`$SHELL -il`, TERM, 80x24, the backend's cwd, `/bin/sh` fallback) - the test injects `shell: process.env.SHELL`, `cwd: process.cwd()`, `env: process.env` and leaves the constants where `PtyLiveSessions` holds them, so it exercises the closed configuration rather than a hermetic one of its own; P-7 (the scrollback is the second subscriber's first frame) - test 2 relies on exactly that; P-9 (`session-not-live`) - not exercised, correctly, because `conventions/testing.md` rule 3 gives the refusals to the layer that owns them and leaves the happy path to the edge; D-10 (everything new under `backend/` is TypeScript) - the new file is `.ts` with relative imports naming the real `.ts` extension. The change to `plugin/scripts/ct-step.mjs` touches no row: D-12 and D-19 reserve sequencing to `run-machine.js` and the change is in a scope control, not in step order. No row is implemented with a different value and none is reopened.

Exemplars. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/tool-runner-real-process.test.ts` - the diff plays the same role and matches its idiom: a type holding the test's helpers (`Node` there, `RealTerminals`/`RunningApi`/`SseFrames`/`Echo` here), a budget constant rather than a sleep, `afterEach` cleanup, and the `-real-process` suffix. `backend/__tests__/infrastructure/sessions-route.test.ts` - the new `RunningApi` is a near-literal imitation of that file's (`static readonly #started`, `stopAll` with `splice(0)`, the same `#NO_FRONTEND`/`#NO_EVENTS`, the same `port: 0` construction and the same field list), which is the repo's established shape across the eleven test files that build an `ApiServer`; the duplication is that idiom, not a decision spread, and `conventions/decisions.md` explicitly leaves boundary idiom to the rule of three. Rules. `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: every identifier, test name and diagnostic string in the diff is English, no product copy is involved. `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`: the new module is `.ts`, imports name the real extension, and its 'a failing test must not leak a process' rule is met - `afterEach` does `await RunningApi.stopAll()` then `realTerminals.killAll()`, and I checked `ApiServer.stop()` (api-server.ts:288) never rejects (`server.close(resolve)` plus `closeAllConnections()`), so the kill is always reached even when an assertion failed. `conventions/testing.md`: the assertions are the literal payloads at the boundary (`toEqual({sessions:[...]})`, `toEqual({status:'typed',id})`) and the SSE frame is hand-parsed from the wire rather than composed with `SessionStreamRoute.frameFor`, which is what that document asks; both assertions can fail for the reason their names give. `conventions/style.md`: the new backend file carries no comment at all and every function hangs off a type; the comments added to `plugin/scripts/ct-step.mjs` and to `plugin/__tests__/ct-step-plan-and-checks.test.js` follow the host's style in modules that are already written that way, which `CLAUDE.md` keeps exempt for the no-prose rule specifically ('The yardstick's other two rules - no prose in the code, and no free function at module level - keep their exemption here'), and neither places a new concept in an old file to inherit it. `conventions/simplicity.md`: nothing added lacks a caller; the ct-step change is one `filter`. `conventions/architecture.md`: no production module is added, no layer is crossed, and `Echo` is the sanctioned namespace-class ('A class nobody instantiates is a namespace, tolerated only because conventions/style.md bans loose functions'). `conventions/boundaries.md`/`domain.md`: no new port, value object or adapter. Delivery: no document of either yardstick prescribes a shape of delivery for adding an end-to-end test, and no signature or public contract is altered, so this item is silent there. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) CLOSED VOCABULARY - the only classifying value in the diff is the wire `status`, asserted as the literal `'typed'` against the frozen vocabulary the input route owns; there is no dispatch and no catch-all branch anywhere in the diff; it passes. (2) RAW MAP AS THE RETURN VALUE OF LOGIC - no production logic is added; the only multi-field returns are `RunningApi.openedOn`'s `{port, session}` and the three wire-shaped types, which are a declared TypeScript record consumed by destructuring in the same file and serialization payloads respectively, both of which that document names as the legitimate case; it passes. (3) TWO FIELDS THAT HAVE TO AGREE / SENTINEL - no subject: the two empty strings in the diff (`#buffer`, `held.seen`) are concatenation accumulators, not an absence wearing a value's clothes, and no flag repeats what another field says. (4) AN ERROR NAMED FOR WHERE IT HAPPENS - the three thrown errors are named for what happened ('the stream ended before a full frame arrived', 'this suite never streams plan events', and the budget's message which quotes the token and what was seen), none for a module; it passes.

The diff's `-` lines are four, all in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-issue-327-the-session-channel.md`: the old `**Files:**` line, the sentence 'No code - this task adds one test file; every module it exercises was built in Tasks 1 to 9.', and the opening of the `**Tests:**` line. None is an assertion, a case or a test. Both test files in the diff are pure additions (`session-channel-real-process.test.ts` is `new file mode`, and the hunk in `plugin/__tests__/ct-step-plan-and-checks.test.js` adds a block and removes nothing). I checked the `**Tests:**` rewrite specifically, since an amendment that drops a promised test name reaches the judge unchecked: both names the plan originally promised survive verbatim and one is added beside them. Nothing pre-existing ended up asserting less.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced entirely by production code the earlier tasks committed and the test reaches it through real HTTP: a real `ApiServer` listening on a real port, a real `PtyLiveSessions` over the real `node-pty` spawn, and `fetch` as the client. Nothing on the path under test is doubled: the only stand-ins in the arrange are `ReviewsSpy`, `PlanSessions` and a `PlanEvents` whose `read` rejects, and they belong to endpoints this test never calls - they exist because `ApiServer`'s constructor demands every collaborator by name, which is the shape `sessions-route.test.ts` already uses. No expected value is hard-coded: the ids and names asserted are read off the `LiveSession` the adapter really returned, and the token asserted on the stream is one the pty really printed. There is no line of behaviour living in the test's scaffolding with no production line behind it.

The four staged paths all appear in the amended `**Files:**`, which the program already crossed against the index. What is mine is the plan hunk and what was written inside the files. THE AMENDMENT, line by line: it ADDS two rows to the section 6 table, two paths to `**Files:**`, one `Contract` block, one test name to `**Tests:**` (keeping both originals verbatim), one verification command (keeping both originals verbatim), and assumption 13; it REMOVES only the sentence 'No code - this task adds one test file', which the amendment itself makes false. Nothing was rewritten into a command that passes and no promised test name was dropped - the two shapes of disarming the rubric warns reach me unchecked. Assumption 13 is prose in the file this task's `**Files:**` declares `(modify)` for exactly that purpose, and I verified its claim against `backend/API.md:735-738`, which does say a session that exits is not reopened. THE CHANGE TO THE RUN MACHINE, judged on its merits rather than on the story: I confirmed the deadlock from the source, not from the report. `declaredScope` compares `t.files` against `workPathsInTheIndex()`, and `ct-step.mjs:1430` filters `planRelPath()` out of that set unconditionally, so a `**Files:**` naming the plan's own path can never satisfy the second loop; the failure is pushed unconditionally and `controlsVerb` (line 1346-1350) sets `OUTCOMES.FAILED` with no report-based waiver, so the printed advice 'say it in your report and leave the path in the plan' does not clear it; and `amendmentOnlyAdds` (line 1528) refuses the removal. No state satisfied both halves. The repair is one line, and it is symmetric with two exemptions already in the same module: line 1430 on the touched side and line 1295, where `report` already excludes `planRelPath()` from the very same declared-versus-touched comparison. It cannot weaken scope for any other path - the two loops still cross every other declared and every other touched path in full, and the only path it drops is the one the program stages (line 1187) and commits itself and that `amendmentOnlyAdds` guards byte-for-byte against HEAD. The comment is true on each of its claims, which I checked against lines 1187, 1295, 1430 and 1528. The new plugin test pins it: it declares `plan.md` in a `**Files:**`, reports only `uno.txt`, and asserts `controls: done` with the log not naming `plan.md` - revert the filter and the second loop fires 'is not among what was touched', which is `controls: failed` and a log that names it. I searched the plugin for anything else that depends on the old behaviour: `declaredScope`'s declared-versus-touched branch is exercised only in `ct-step-plan-and-checks.test.js`, and in every other fixture the filter is a no-op, so the narrowed verification command does cover what changed; CI's `test` job runs the plugin's whole suite on the pull request in any case, and `scripts/ct-step.mjs` is not an input to any committed bundle (`dist-matches-sources.test.js` lists `scripts/ct-step-commit.js`), so the `dist` job is unaffected. Saying plainly what was asked: I do not report this as a defect. `CLAUDE.md` prescribes this exact route - 'A control that refuses when it should not is a finding, not an obstacle. Stop, say what refused and why you believe it is wrong, and let a person decide' - and the run stopped in `blocked-controls` instead of routing around either half. The uncomfortable fact, stated so the human at the pull request sees it rather than finds it: the controls that cleared this task ran the patched machine, and the patch's whole effect is that the control stopped demanding the plan's own path; the other three paths of this diff were still crossed against `**Files:**` in full. One residue, reported here and not as a finding because the implementer's narrative is settled before me: `## Rutas tocadas` names only two of the four staged paths, so the report under-declared the two plugin files - `report` warns on precisely that mismatch (line 1295-1297) and stages what was measured, `declaredScope` then measured the index, and both files are declared loudly in the amended plan, so nothing travelled hidden.

Three new tests: two in `session-channel-real-process.test.ts` and one in `ct-step-plan-and-checks.test.js`. DETERMINISTIC: no clock or date in any assertion - the 30s budget is a failure budget with a diagnostic message, not an assertion about time, and there is no sleep standing in for synchronisation anywhere; the test reads frames until the token arrives, which is the shape that does not flake. No network beyond loopback, port 0 so no fixed port is taken for granted, `#NO_FRONTEND` under `tmpdir()`, and the plugin test builds its repo with `mkdtempSync`. `randomUUID` is used for ids but no assertion is on a literal id: the expected value is read off the `LiveSession` the adapter returned. ISOLATED: `realTerminals` is rebuilt in `beforeEach` and every pty it opened is killed in `afterEach`; `RunningApi.#started` is static but `stopAll` splices it empty in the same hook, and I checked `ApiServer.stop()` cannot reject, so the kill after it is always reached - including after a failed assertion, which is what `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` demands by name. Neither test depends on the other's order or state. VERIFIES REAL BEHAVIOUR: every assertion is on what real production code did over real HTTP - the listing built from the adapter's own map, the bytes the pty really printed, the 202 the real input route answered, and in the plugin test the real `ct-step` subprocess's stdout and control log; none is on a mock's call count, a stub's return or a constant the test just defined, and none would survive its subject being broken. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` before weighing anything beyond those three. Two things I considered under it and am deliberately not reporting. Its table says "Minimal | One thing. 'and' in name? Split it", and `it('the live session is listed, its stream carries what it prints and what is typed reaches it')` joins three behaviours - but the plan's `**Tests:**` prescribes that exact string and `ct-step controls` searches the staged files for it literally, so splitting it would put the task red; that is a control of the plan clashing with the text the implementer was handed, and the only diff it could have written. Second, the token matched on the stream is the two-character `ct`, which `conventions/testing.md` would call matching loose where a distinctive one was available; the risk it carries is a false pass rather than a flake, and the plan itself wrote both the input `echo ct\r` and the token `ct` into the task's text, so it is the plan's word and not the implementer's choice.
